newsitem.title: FINLAND: FINNISH NOV M2 FALL UNDRAMATIC, DEC SEEN DOWN TOO.
newsitem.headline: FINNISH NOV M2 FALL UNDRAMATIC, DEC SEEN DOWN TOO.

text.p: A return to a negative Finnish M2 money supply figure in November came as no surprise and December M2 is likely to show a fall as well, analysts said on Wednesday.
The Bank of Finland said M2 fell 1.2 percent year-on-year in November having risen 0.3 percent in October after being in the red throughout most of 1996.
"The figure is undramatic," a central bank official said.
The M2 money aggregate comprises money in circulation, cheques, giro and transaction accounts as well as fixed-term and other bank deposits held by the public.

M2 fell into negative territory in November and is likely to show a bigger fall in December due to a big flow of funds into fixed-term bank deposits in November-December 1995, the central bank official said.

At end-1996 there was also an outflow of funds from expiring fixed-term bank deposits, he said. This view was supported by a slower increase in the narrow M1 money aggregate -- to 17.2 percent in November from 19.8 percent in October.
"I think a lot of money poured into the bourse, mainly through unit trusts at the end of 1996," said an economist at a commercial bank. "The (M2) figure was not surprising," he said.
